judge: Nora — self-published romantic-fantasy novelist, eleven books, running her own author business solo, mostly from her phone. Judging KIRA OS on branch claude/kira-ux-women-users as the code actually is.
first_five_minutes:
Cassy opens the link on her phone. The login page is genuinely lovely — Cormorant italic, "A little more room to be the author," a verified Brontë line with a Gutenberg source. It says "WELCOME HOME, CASSANDRA" and, in the small print under the password field, "Private access, by invitation" (components/kira/login-form.tsx:56). Nobody invited her; Michael added her account by hand and the app elsewhere insists it never sends invitations. First tiny wrong note, and she won't be able to name it. She signs in. Connected home: "Welcome home, Cassandra." Good. A quote. An idea shelf. A "Start with one small thing" checklist with three numbered steps — she will click one, come back, and find all three still showing "01 02 03" with no checkmark, because `complete` is hardcoded `false` (components/kira/getting-started.tsx:81,89,97). A to-do list that never lets her finish is a small daily insult. If Michael shows her the demo build instead, the home screen says "Good afternoon, Cassandra." at whatever hour it is (components/kira/mission-control.tsx:38 — no clock, just a string). Six metric cards with DEMO badges she cannot read: the badge is 7px, and inside the metric cards on her phone it drops to 5px (app/globals.css:554, 2333-2334). Then the second card down, in big serif on her iPhone: "A few thingsneed your instinct." — the `
` is hidden at ≤1020px (app/globals.css:2111) and JSX ate the space (components/kira/mission-control.tsx:72-74). That is the first typography-grade defect she sees, on the hero card, on the screen she is being shown the app on. If her desk were empty it would say "The minions are working. Go write. 🖤" (mission-control.tsx:94). First real click: "Take your seat" → Cassandra's Desk. Heading: "They bring the evidence. You bring the instinct." She will ask who "they" are. Nobody is running. The first brief in the list is written about her in the third person — "First confirm audience fit with Cassandra" (lib/data/seed.ts:284). She is reading a memo about herself, in her own workspace, named after her pen name. If she gets as far as Marketing Plans, she builds a plan for her own books, saves it, and reads: "Michael can review this plan and activate its tasks. You can keep exploring while it awaits review." (components/kira/plans-page.tsx:104). That is the moment I would lose her. Eleven books, her business, her name on the sidebar — and she needs her friend's sign-off to turn on her own 30/60/90 calendar. What would actually win her: the book page. Warm, calm, "Your book, in your words," an explicit permission checkbox before her manuscript goes anywhere, spoilers off by default, every finding traceable to a passage. That page is the product. It is also the page where she cannot delete the file she just gave it.

scores.verdict: The app is branded with her pen name and addressed to her by name, but she is an Editor in someone else's workspace. Her own marketing plan for her own books cannot be activated without Michael, by name, in the UI. She cannot see who else can read her workspace, cannot manage access, and cannot remove her own manuscript. Six separate surfaces tell her to ask the owner.

top_findings.title: Her own marketing plan needs Michael's approval, and the UI says so by name
top_findings.problem: Cassy is an Editor. When she builds a marketing plan for her own books, it lands in "Needs owner review" (line 14) and the page tells her "Michael can review this plan and activate its tasks." The approve/activate controls are owner-only (line 103). This is the central Bumble-lens failure: the workspace carries her pen name in the sidebar, addresses her by name on every page, and then requires a man's sign-off to switch on her own 30/60/90 calendar. The name is also hardcoded, so it is wrong for any other deployment.
top_findings.proposed_change: Tonight: replace the hardcoded name with the owner identity from the access API and explain the gate and her options — "This plan is waiting on {owner} to review its budget and dates before the tasks go live. You can keep editing it, generate a revision, or work the steps yourself without activating them." Then the owner decides the real question: either make Cassy the workspace Owner before the demo (one row change, and the honest answer given whose business this is), or keep the review gate but scope it to what it is actually for — spend and dated commitments — and let her activate zero-budget plans herself.
top_findings.owner_decision_needed: Whether Cassy should be Owner rather than Editor, and if not, whether the review gate applies to all plans or only to ones with a budget. The wording of the gate is code; who holds the gate is Michael's call and should be made before she sees this tomorrow.

top_findings.title: She cannot take her manuscript back
top_findings.problem: There is no delete path for a manuscript anywhere in the product. app/api/library/[bookId]/route.ts exposes only GET and PATCH; app/api/manuscripts/* has upload, process, reading and source, and no DELETE handler exists outside the connections routes. She uploads the most intimate file she owns, an AI gateway reads it (lib/manuscripts/provider.ts:24), passages and embeddings and extracted knowledge are persisted, and the only controls offered are pause, resume and retry. Meanwhile the ads surface offers "Disconnect & delete imported reports" (components/kira/ads/dashboard.tsx:45). Facebook spend data can be withdrawn; her novel cannot.
top_findings.proposed_change: Add a DELETE route at /api/manuscripts/[id] under the same role and tenant checks as upload, cascading to chunks, embeddings and book_intelligence, and surface a "Remove this manuscript" button in the library-actions row beside Pause/Retry. The confirm dialog should itemise what goes (the stored file, its passages, its embeddings, everything Kira extracted) and what stays (the book record, and any desk brief she already saved that quotes it). If it cannot ship tonight, change line 118 from "Add your manuscript once." to say plainly that uploading is not yet reversible from this screen.

top_findings.title: "Private to your workspace" is not what she will hear, and every viewer can read her manuscript
top_findings.problem: The manuscript card says "Private to your workspace. Your manuscript is never rewritten." She will read "private" as "only me." In fact every workspace member can read it: in connected-book-detail.tsx, `canEdit` (line 29) gates only upload and metadata editing — the knowledge section (line 130), the source-passage dialog (line 138) and the spoiler-gated manuscript search (line 135) are not role-gated, so a Viewer can pull up verbatim excerpts. And she cannot even see the member list, because access-page.tsx:120 renders it for owners only. The consent checkbox she ticks (connected-book-detail.tsx:119) also names no AI provider and no retention period, just "Kira's AI services".
top_findings.proposed_change: Three changes, all code. (a) Rewrite line 67: "Only people with access to this workspace can read it — today that is {n} people, listed under Workspace access. It is never public, and it is never used to train a model." (b) Show `access.owner` and `access.members` read-only to non-owners in access-page.tsx, keeping grant/revoke owner-only. (c) Expand the consent line to name the processor and retention, sourcing the provider name from the same config that produces `knowledge.model`.

top_findings.title: The type scale bottoms out at 5px, and the DEMO badge is the victim
top_findings.problem: 220 CSS rules set a font-size under 12px. The worst are load-bearing honesty and consent copy: `.origin-badge` (the DEMO marker) is 7px at line 554 and 5px inside metric cards on mobile at line 2334; `.cover-placeholder` ("CATALOG PLACEHOLDER · NOT OFFICIAL COVER") is 5px at line 1453; `.status-pill` is 7px at line 1229; `.quiet-note` — which carries the consent explanations, the spoiler counts, the "nothing is published or sent" reassurances and every viewer-role note — is 10px at line 1135 and 9px at line 1746. On her phone, the six impressive numbers on the home screen carry a 5px DEMO badge, which is to say they look real. This is simultaneously the biggest accessibility defect (WCAG 1.4.4, 1.4.12) and the biggest honesty defect, because the honesty system is implemented entirely in the unreadable band.
top_findings.proposed_change: Set an 11px floor for any text that is not purely ornamental, and 13px for `.quiet-note`. Specifically: 554 → 11px, 1229 → 11px, 1135 → 13px, delete 1746, 1453 → 9px, and delete the mobile overrides at 2034, 2211, 2334 and 2546. Then re-check the six-badge assertion in tests/e2e/workspace.spec.ts (it asserts presence in the "Demo metrics" region, not size, so it will stay green) and re-run the axe checks for the new layout.

top_findings.title: "A few thingsneed your instinct." on the home hero, at every phone and tablet width
top_findings.problem:
The heading is authored as `A few things
need your instinct.`. At ≤1020px, app/globals.css:2111 sets `.desk-preview h2 br { display: none; }`, and JSX strips the whitespace around the newline, so the words collide: "A few thingsneed your instinct." It renders in 30px Cormorant on the second card of the connected and demo home pages. Confirmed in the captured mobile-home screenshot.
top_findings.proposed_change:
`A few things{" "}
need your instinct.` — one character. Then grep the other `
`-in-heading patterns (desk-page.tsx:42, universe-catalog.tsx:56, settings-page.tsx:50, studio-page.tsx:177, learn-page.tsx:141, connections-page.tsx:89) for the same collapse risk under their own media queries.

top_findings.title: "The minions are working" and "They bring the evidence" invent a staff that does not exist
top_findings.problem: Three strings assert autonomous activity. mission-control.tsx:94 and desk-page.tsx:110 both say "The minions are working. Go write. 🖤" when her desk is clear. desk-page.tsx:41-45 heads her decision page with "They bring the evidence. You bring the instinct." and "teach the team what only you know." agent-status.tsx:18 labels six specialists "YOUR BUSINESS TEAM" with live-looking WAITING/IDLE pills, undercut by a disclaimer in the smallest text on the card. Nothing is running. This violates the project's own rule against fabricated agent status, and "minions" is a cartoon metaphor aimed at a professional with eleven books out.
top_findings.proposed_change: mission-control.tsx:94 and desk-page.tsx:110 → "Nothing needs you right now. Go write." (no emoji). desk-page.tsx:41 → "The evidence is here."; line 45 → "Approve, adjust, or record what only you know." agent-status.tsx:18 → "PLANNED SPECIALISTS · NOT RUNNING", and change the status pills from WAITING/IDLE to "Demo only" / "Not built yet". None of these strings are pinned by tests/e2e/workspace.spec.ts or experience.spec.ts.

top_findings.title: Her unfinished drafts live only in memory and will not survive her phone
top_findings.problem: `scratchpad`, `learnScratchpad` and `studioScratchpad` are re-created fresh on every mount and never persisted; only committed workspace records reach localStorage. The protections built around this are careful — a beforeunload guard (line 471), a sign-out confirmation dialog (app-shell.tsx:420), keep-or-replace prompts, and honest labels like "Not saved yet · Kept while you explore. Save before reloading or signing out." But beforeunload does not fire when iOS Safari discards a backgrounded tab, and Cassy is on her phone half the day. She will lose a half-written launch brief and the app will have warned her in 10px text.
top_findings.proposed_change: Persist the scratchpads to sessionStorage under a key namespaced by `viewerEmail`, restore on mount, clear in `clearPrivateScratchpads`, and wrap every access in try/catch so blocked storage degrades to today's behaviour. sessionStorage is per-tab and dies with it, so no private workspace record outlives the session — but confirm the scope against rule 12 before shipping. Then soften manual-review-form.tsx:228 to "Not saved yet · Kept in this browser tab. Save it to keep it for good."
top_findings.owner_decision_needed: Whether per-tab sessionStorage for unsaved private drafts is acceptable under the rule that private workspace state must not live in browser storage. The code change is trivial; the policy call is Michael's.

top_findings.title: A getting-started checklist that can never be completed
top_findings.problem: The three onboarding steps each hardcode `complete: false` (lines 81, 89, 97). The completion rendering is fully built — a Check icon, a `learning-step-complete` class and an sr-only "Complete:" prefix at line 127 — and can never fire. The component already computes `ideas` and `decisions` counts at lines 73-74 and uses them for the status text, so the real signal is sitting right there unused. Every visit tells her she has not started.
top_findings.proposed_change: Step 2 `complete: ideas > 0`, step 3 `complete: decisions > 0`, and step 1 from a lightweight localStorage breadcrumb set when a book detail page opens (the file already owns a localStorage preference helper). Not pinned by any e2e test.

top_findings.title: Error toast shows a green checkmark; error page describes the wrong storage mode
top_findings.problem: The toast renders `<Check size={16} />` unconditionally, including when `state.error` is set and `role="alert"` fires — so every failure message is preceded by a success tick. Separately, app/error.tsx:9 tells the user "Your locally saved decisions are still in your browser," which is false in connected mode where everything lives in Supabase; the boundary renders in both modes and cannot read the store.
top_findings.proposed_change: app-shell.tsx:404 → `{state.error ? <TriangleAlert size={16} aria-hidden="true" /> : <Check size={16} aria-hidden="true" />}`. app/error.tsx:9 → "Nothing you saved has been lost. Try loading this workspace again."

top_findings.title: Seeded briefs talk about her in the third person, in her own desk
top_findings.problem: The demo briefs she will read tomorrow are written about her: "First confirm audience fit with Cassandra" (seed.ts:284), "Test the positioning only after Cassandra confirms audience fit" (seed.ts:179), "Next: Cassandra verifies book relevance and audience fit" (demo-store.tsx:318), "Cassandra's verification" (book-detail.tsx:205), "Cassandra's audience guidance" (app/[module]/page.tsx:17). She is the only reader of these. It is the clearest tell that the copy was written for a stakeholder demo rather than for the woman using it.
top_findings.proposed_change: Rewrite in second person: "First confirm audience fit yourself, then verify which books actually fit"; "…only after you confirm audience fit and book relevance"; "Next: confirm book relevance and audience fit, then choose approved assets"; "your verification"; "Your audience guidance". Unit tests in tests/ pin seed copy, and regeneration needs `npm run db:seed:generate`; do both in one change.

top_findings.title: Raw enums, internal version numbers and a JSON dump reach the UI
top_findings.problem: plans-page.tsx:111 renders `JSON.stringify(...)` inside a `<pre>` for every saved generation. approval-card.tsx:78 prints the bare status enum (`pending`, lowercase). approval-card.tsx:85 shows "VERSION {version + 1}". access-page.tsx:109 prints "Your role: editor". settings-page.tsx:90 says "blocked in Phase One". ads/dashboard.tsx:45 shows her the literal token `ads_read`. These are the seams where the builder's mental model shows through.
top_findings.proposed_change: Replace the JSON block with a rendered summary (revision, model, cost, intent, evidence labels) plus a download link for the raw snapshot. Map status and role enums to sentence-case display strings. "VERSION n+1" → "Draft n+1". "blocked in Phase One" → "Nothing in this workspace can post, send, or spend. That is not a setting." Replace `ads_read` with "read-only access to your ad results".

top_findings.title: "Private access, by invitation" promises a flow that does not exist
top_findings.problem: The login page's closing line says access is "by invitation." The access page says the opposite twice — "This adds permission only... No invitation or email is sent" (access-page.tsx:122) and "Access saved. No invitation or email was sent" (line 84) — and the project rules forbid sending any auth email. The first sentence Cassy reads about how she got here is untrue.
top_findings.proposed_change: "Private access. Your workspace owner adds accounts by hand — no invitations are sent." Not pinned by any test.

top_findings.title: Screen readers never hear the pending-decision count, or the nav descriptions
top_findings.problem: The desk nav Link carries `aria-label="Cassandra's Desk"`, which overrides its entire subtree — so the count badge's own `aria-label={count} pending decisions` at line 155 is silently discarded and never announced. Separately, every nav item's explanatory `<small>` is `aria-hidden="true"` (lines 134 and 166), so screen-reader users get "The Universe", "The Raven", "The Hunt" with no gloss, while sighted users get "Your books", "Evidence & recommendations to review", and so on. The axe checks pass because neither is a rule violation — they are correct-by-the-letter choices that hand blind users the harder product.
top_findings.proposed_change: Remove the `aria-label` from each nav Link so the name computes from content; drop `aria-hidden` from the descriptions; change the badge to `{count} decisions need your eye`. tests/e2e/workspace.spec.ts locates nav items by accessible name — re-run and update the selectors in the same change.

top_findings.title: No light theme exists, and "Good afternoon" is a constant
top_findings.problem: 3,688 lines of CSS contain no `prefers-color-scheme` block and no theme attribute — the workspace is dark, permanently, with no toggle. And mission-control.tsx:38 hardcodes "Good afternoon, Cassandra." with no clock anywhere in the codebase (the only matches for `getHours`/`morning`/`evening` are zero). She will open it at 9pm.
top_findings.proposed_change: Add a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light)` override for the `:root` tokens plus the hardcoded hex values in `.quiet-note` and its neighbours, and give `body` an explicit background in both. For the greeting, derive morning/afternoon/evening from the server-supplied `dateKey` timezone. tests/e2e/workspace.spec.ts pins the literal heading "Good afternoon, Cassandra." — update it to a fixed-clock fixture or a /Good (morning|afternoon|evening), Cassandra\./ pattern in the same change.
top_findings.owner_decision_needed: Whether a light theme ships before the demo or after. The dark aesthetic is a deliberate brand choice and a light variant needs a real design pass, not just token inversion — worth asking Cassy directly which she prefers rather than guessing.

what_works: The manuscript consent model. connected-book-detail.tsx:119 requires an explicit checkbox naming both the permission and its limit ("This does not approve publishing excerpts") and refuses the upload without it (line 81). Spoilers default to off in both the knowledge workbench (book-knowledge.tsx:46) and the manuscript search (connected-book-detail.tsx:27), and the hidden count is shown so she knows what she is not seeing (book-knowledge.tsx:89). Do not weaken any of this.

Traceability from every finding back to her own words. Each extracted fact and character carries a "Read supporting passage" button (connected-book-detail.tsx:108) that opens the verbatim source, and the framing at line 131 is honest about what a matched quotation does and does not prove. book-knowledge.tsx separates "Manuscript-supported · unreviewed" from "Interpretation · verify with source" on every item (line 102).

Background reading that respects her time and her connection. Pause, resume and retry are all first-class (connected-book-detail.tsx:129), progress is persisted per passage, "you can leave this screen or close the tab" is stated plainly (line 126), and failure modes are explained in terms of what is safe rather than error codes (line 125, 128).

The draft-protection choreography throughout. Every place where an action could overwrite unfinished words asks first and states that nothing has changed yet: the idea-shelf prefill (manual-review-form.tsx:139-157), the book-details starter (book-detail.tsx:216-221), the Michael starter in the workshop (learn-page.tsx:158), the new-question reset in Studio (studio-page.tsx:206), and sign-out (app-shell.tsx:420-427). The guard at demo-store.tsx:252 that refuses to clear a scratchpad if she typed more after submitting is the kind of detail almost nobody builds.

Provenance as a first-class visual system. The DemoBadge / origin-badge component tags every synthetic record, the evidence drawer shows source, type, retrieval date and source ID with a link to the original (evidence-drawer.tsx:42-70), the demo refresh notice says "No live sources were queried" (demo-store.tsx:355), and the creative-firewall panel explicitly warns that "Allowed describes policy permission, not an implemented feature" (settings-page.tsx:88). Keep every one of these strings.

Cost and model transparency in Ask Raven. studio-page.tsx:203 shows the model name and estimated dollar cost per answer, line 188 states the daily cap and that there are no automatic retries, and line 185 tells her exactly what leaves her workspace ("Only this question is sent to the AI provider"). The Plans surface does the same at plans-page.tsx:92.

Version-conflict handling on decisions. approval-card.tsx:41 detects that a brief changed while the dialog was open and blocks the save with a plain-language explanation at line 210, and the store reconciles rather than guessing (demo-store.tsx:218-229). This is the kind of correctness that stops a shared workspace from quietly losing someone's work.

The role-degradation messaging. Every write surface has a specific, non-punitive viewer-access note that distinguishes "you have viewer access" from "we could not check your permissions" and always reassures her that her unfinished work survives (manual-review-form.tsx:130, approval-card.tsx:143, learn-page.tsx:188, book-detail.tsx:138, demo-store.tsx:129). The WorkspacePermissionNotice with a retry and focus restoration (workspace-permission-notice.tsx) is a genuinely good pattern.

The inspiration and lesson content. lib/data/inspiration.ts is written as real editorial questions for a working author — "Which published book would you love to put back in a reader's hands?" — with a first step, a structured brief template, and no fabricated claims about reader behaviour. The daily quote is verified against Gutenberg with a dated verification field, an excerpt flag, and in-book context (inspiration.ts:126-164). lib/data/agent-recipes.ts bakes the creative firewall and the source-checking discipline directly into every generated prompt (agent-recipes.ts:99-101).

The typography and palette. Cormorant Garamond against Manrope, the wine/olive/gold accents, the hand-built book covers with their own ornament and placeholder disclaimer, the raven illustration. It reads like a hardback rather than a dashboard, which is exactly right for this person. Fix the sizes; do not touch the taste.

Focus management after async work. Errors, notices and dialogs consistently move focus somewhere useful and return it to the trigger afterward — approval-card.tsx:167-175, access-page.tsx:149-155, desk-page.tsx:21-31, getting-started.tsx:65,70, learn-page.tsx:91. Combined with the skip link, the reduced-motion block (globals.css:2689) and the 44px mobile input floor (globals.css:3678), there is a real accessibility foundation here to build the type-size fix on top of.
